entries.author: Identity-MD field notes
entries.title: A swarm in the sky. A feed on the ground.
entries.text:
Identity-MD brings a community of contributors together to build in public. Signal puts the conversations, ideas and things they make in one chronological feed.

This is an illustrative entry, written to demonstrate the reader. The project’s live website describes a contributor network: one swarm seat per Identity.MD NFT. Contributors connect an agent to take jobs and earn.

Open the project website for current information. This preview is not an announcement from the Identity-MD team.
entries.imageAlt: A green geometric network: a swarm in the sky.

entries.author: A swarm contributor
entries.title: Good ideas should travel further than the timeline.
entries.text:
The best part of building around Identity-MD? Seeing someone pick up an idea, add their own perspective, and turn it into something useful. More context, fewer ticker-only posts.

A good feed should preserve that context. Original posts belong here; repeated copies, replies without context, and engagement bait do not.

This example shows how a substantive top-level post expands without sending you to another tab.

entries.author: Open network notes
entries.title: A small case for quieter feeds
entries.text:
Following $IMD should not mean scrolling through the same post twelve times. Give me the original, enough context to understand it, and the choice to keep reading.

Signal’s collector compares normalized text and canonical links before publishing an entry. Similar copies are grouped around the earliest available original.

Memes and images still have a place. A short caption is not the same thing as a low-effort post.

entries.author: The open notebook
entries.title: What does it mean to build in public?
entries.text:
A practical look at the small habits that make an open contributor network work: share the attempt, document the decisions, and leave something useful behind.

For an Identity-MD contributor, a useful artifact might be a tool, a piece of research, or a website. The common thread is work that another person can inspect and build on.

This illustrative article demonstrates long-form reading in the feed. Full imported text is shown when the source provides it; excerpts are identified and linked to their original.

entries.author: Around the ecosystem
entries.title: One project, many places to follow it
entries.text:
From contributor notes to project explainers, a useful Identity-MD story can start almost anywhere.

RSS and Atom sources can be added to the collector alongside the supported social APIs. Platform access depends on each source’s public feeds and API terms.

This preview story demonstrates an expandable entry from another website.

entries.author: A builder’s notes
entries.title: The small details are the product.
entries.text:
Readable text. Useful filters. An undo button. Making the Identity-MD conversation easier to follow starts with getting the ordinary things right.

This is a sample community post. Try saving it, hiding it, switching the layout, or filtering to a single source. Your reading preferences stay in this browser.
